confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on two web searches. One looked up the RBA exchange rate and one looked up crowd-sourced cost-of-living figures for Wollongong, mainly from My Life Elsewhere. Those figures put an inexpensive meal at about A$23–26, a cappuccino at A$4.60–5.60 and a pint at A$8.60–9.10. Their pages disagree with each other and their dates are unclear, so I raised them slightly to allow for inflation to the July 2026 window. The mid-range meal for two is my own estimate, set against typical Australian regional-city prices. I estimated cocktail and wine prices from their usual relationship to beer prices in Australia, because I did not find direct local figures for them. I estimated the accommodation anchors from general knowledge only, without checking any listings. They assume July winter off-season demand. Wollongong has few hostels, so the hostel figures are the least certain. The FX observation is the latest RBA figure I could find (18 Nov 2026). It comes from an RBA feed snippet reported in search results, not from a direct read of the table.
comparable_city_reasoning: I treated Wollongong as a regional NSW coastal city close to Sydney. I placed its dining prices at about the Australian average, slightly below Sydney. I placed its accommodation below Sydney and similar to Newcastle NSW and Geelong in the off-season.
